memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So they went up to Joseph's steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house. 'We beg your pardon, our lord,' they said, 'we came down here the first time to buy food. But at the place where we stopped for the night we opened our sacks and each of us found his silver—the exact weight—in the mouth of his sack. So we have brought it back with us. We have also brought additional silver with us to buy food. We don't know who put our silver in our sacks.'" - Gen 43:19-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Fearing they will be accused of theft, the brothers take the initiative. Rather than waiting to be confronted, they go to Joseph's steward and explain everything about the returned silver: "We found it in our sacks... we don't know who put it there... we have brought it back." They come clean, offering full honesty and even restoring the money they could have kept.

This is a healthy instinct, and a sign of their changing hearts. Instead of hiding, covering up, or hoping the matter would go unnoticed, they bring the whole thing into the open. They would rather face the truth head-on than live under the shadow of a hidden problem. The men who once buried their sin now choose transparency.

There is wisdom here for us. When something is unresolved — a debt, a misunderstanding, a wrong — the temptation is to say nothing and hope it disappears. But hidden things weigh on us and often come out worse later. It is far better to take the initiative, come clean, and deal honestly with the matter, trusting God with the outcome.

Is there something you have been quietly hoping no one will notice — money owed, a wrong done, a truth avoided? Consider the brothers' example. Take the initiative to make it right. Come clean, restore what you can, speak the truth. A clear conscience is worth more than the false safety of concealment.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something unresolved I'm hoping will just disappear?
2. Do I take the initiative to come clean, or wait to be confronted?
3. What matter do I need to bring honestly into the open?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the courage to come clean rather than hide. Where there is something unresolved, help me to take the initiative, deal honestly, and make it right, trusting You with the outcome. Amen.
